messages:
Maya Chen: FYI incident-bot just paged us for a sustained SLO burn on /api/generate. Seeing a 12h elevated window, customers noticing latency spikes. Can oncall grab this?
incident-bot: ALERT: service: /api/generate | SLO burn-rate: 4.6 (multi-window) | affected: 11% of requests | severity: high | runbook: /runbooks/api-latency | ts: 2306019876
Antony Ruiz: oncall here, looking. Any traffic change? release?
Priya Patel: no deploys in the last 24h. Traffic + cache hit drop on redis tier around the same time? pulling logs now.
Jordan Lee: I see multiple 95th spikes aligned with KV-cache misses. Probable cold-cache / cache eviction from a rollout on dedicated.
Maya Chen: ops notes show a Dedicated autoscaler scale-down 6h ago to reclaim nodes. Could be thrash causing cache churn.
Antony Ruiz: ok first step — reduce paging noise. Current pager criteria triggers on 3-window burn >= 4.0. I want to try a temporary change: require sustained burn in the two longest windows AND >10% customers impacted before paging. Thoughts?
Priya Patel: +1 to reduce flapping. But we need a metric for customer-visible errors vs internal SLO. This is latency; customers seeing errors?
Jordan Lee: errors are low, mostly latency. So it's high-severity for some SLAs but probably not P0. Can we change pager severity to P1 for latency-only in this path?
Maya Chen: agree. Action: change pager from immediate P0 to P1 for latency-only if customer error-rate < 1%. Keep P0 for error spikes.
Antony Ruiz: I'll edit the alert rule in grafana-alerts. Proposed patch (temporary):
```yaml
alert: ApiGenerateSloBurn
conditions:
  - multi_window: [1h, 3h, 12h]
  - require: longest_two_windows_sustained
  - impact_threshold: 10% # customers
  - escalate_to: P1
```
Antony Ruiz: pushing change now, will monitor for 15m.
incident-bot: CONFIG_CHANGE: grafana-alerts/ApiGenerateSloBurn updated by Antony Ruiz at 2306020005
Priya Patel: watching dashboards. Also adding a short-lived visual for prefix cache hit rate and leader evictions.
Jordan Lee: creating dashboard panel: "KV cache steady-state" & "dedicated-scaler-events". Linking to thread.
Maya Chen: we should also adjust the multi-window burn detection weights. Current config overly sensitive to the 1h window during traffic bursts. Proposal: weight windows [0.5, 1, 1.5] for [1h,3h,12h]. This favors sustained long-window burns.
Antony Ruiz: agree, less noise. I'll update alert expression to use weighted burn score and set pager threshold to weighted_score >= 2.0.
Priya Patel: note: when you change the shaper, add an explicit TTL so it auto-reverts in 72h unless a runbook ticket exists. Prevent config drift.
Antony Ruiz: good call. Setting revert in 72h.
incident-bot: CHANGE_SCHEDULED: Update includes auto-revert at 72h unless approved.
Jordan Lee: also, customers reporting slow-stream in two enterprise tenants. I'll reach out to AE to confirm impact and add to incident notes.
Maya Chen: handoff plan: Antony will own mitigation for next 2 hours, then Priya takes over the midnight->04:00 UTC window. Leaving a clear checklist in the incident doc.
Antony Ruiz: acknowledged. Checklist being written: 1) confirm grafana change deployed 2) watch weighted burn and customer impact 3) attach dashboard links 4) escalate if errors >1% or weighted_score >3.0
Priya Patel: adding runbook step to check redis memory fragmentation and dedicated pool eviction logs: `kubectl logs -n infra scaler-operator` and `redis-cli info memory`.
Maya Chen: quick note on cost: autoscaler thrash could be caused by aggressive burst policy. Let's flag infra to look at smoother cooldowns after mitigating this incident.
incident-bot: NOTE: paging level downgraded to P1 for latency-only. If error-rate crosses 1% or customer-impact > 25% will escalate to P0.
Jordan Lee: small helpful dashboard snippet for the postmortem: snapshot link: https://grafana.redwood.team/d/SLO-burn-triage?kiosk=tv
Pria (typo) -> Priya Patel: (just a nit) add owners to the dashboard panels so we don't lose context.
Antony Ruiz: logging final state for now: weighted_burn=1.9, customer_impact=9%, error_rate=0.2%. Quietly trending down after autoscaler cooldown. Will monitor for 30m then flip to watch-only.
Maya Chen: after monitoring, we should schedule a noise-reduction follow-up: reduce sensitivity on 1h window, add TTL for temporary changes, document paging criteria changes in oncall runbook, and create a small alert-level decision tree for latency vs error. I'll set a doc and assign owners.
Priya Patel: I'll take the follow-up doc and drive the runbook updates.
Jordan Lee: +1. Also propose a dashboard alert that surfaces "cache eviction storms" as a distinct upstream event to avoid SLO burn misattribution.
Maya Chen: cool. Thanks team — Antony stay on for handoff notes, Priya will pick up later.
OpsPager: Handoff recorded: Antony Ruiz -> Priya Patel at 2306020200.
Maya Chen: closing thread for now, will reopen if anything spikes. :white_check_mark:
